title: Three executable gates and qualification limits
summary: Phase native: forced-GC stale activation and control. Phase bsf: interpreted BSF Java objects, Comparator, Java-thread Runnable. Phase jdorfx: caller-selected genuine sample smoke. Local shell preflight checks passed; installed ooRexx, selected BSF and Ismaili JDORFX archive were unavailable, so runtime and visual tests remain NOT_RUN. On 2026-10-29 a separate mock-only runner contract suite passed three accepted control paths, six negative paths, and opt-in receipt retention. Live ooRexx, BSF and Ismaili JDORFX remain NOT_RUN; CLAUDE-PC's read-only test response identified missing workstation approval/paths.
invariants: Missing runtime inputs fail; never report a silent SKIP/PASS.
Use exact selected dependency paths and versions; no duplicate JAR/native guessing.
Every gate emits and retains its own exact interpreter/build, JAR, JavaFX, sample hashes, logs and exit statuses.
Visual parity must be independently evaluated; production qualification BLOCKED.
A bare zero exit code from a JDORFX sample is insufficient: require a known output marker; sample must reside under the selected source distribution and run from its source directory.
JVM discovery must handle Java alternatives wrappers and an explicit GUI/JavaFX graphics+controls configuration.
Retained evidence is opt-in through EVIDENCE_DIR; mock suite PASS must not be conflated with live runtime or visual approval.

provenance.claim: Mock-only preflight state machine tests, three happy paths and six negative paths
